recommendation.text: On Question 2 (whether to recommend approval of Xiaflex for advanced Dupuytren's Disease), the committee voted unanimously in favor: Yes=12, No=0, Abstain=0.

linkages.concern: During the AdComm, some members felt a registry or post-marketing safety study would be helpful to better characterize the risks of tendon rupture and/or hypersensitivity reactions (other members felt it would add nothing beyond standard pharmacovigilance).
linkages.change: The approval included a REMS (Medication Guide plus Communication Plan) with REMS assessments covering collection and analysis of serious adverse events and the extent of Xiaflex use by physician specialty, to manage the risks of tendon rupture and serious hypersensitivity.

concern_quote.quote: Some members felt that a registry or post-marketing safety study would be helpful to better understand the risks of tendon rupture and/or hypersensitivity reactions. However, other members felt that these studies would not be any more helpful than standard post-marketing vigilance.

change_quote.quote: The clinical review team and the OSE review team have recommended a REMS for Xiaflex in order to ensure that the benefits of the product outweigh the risks of tendon rupture and other serious adverse events affecting the injected extremity, as well as the potential risk of serious hypersensitivity reactions. The REMS should consist of a Medication Guide to inform patients of the potential risks and a Communication Plan to inform health care providers of those risks. The proposed REMS contains a number of REMS assessments that include assessment of the extent of Xiaflex use by physicians of different specialties as well as collection and analysis of serious adverse events occurring with the use of this product.

summary: The Arthritis Advisory Committee (AAC), supplemented by three hand surgeons and two Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee members, met on September 16, 2009 and voted 12-0 to recommend approval of Xiaflex for advanced Dupuytren's Disease. The committee was largely confirmatory: most members judged the proposed clinician training adequate and opinion was divided on whether a registry or post-marketing safety study for tendon rupture/hypersensitivity would add value beyond standard pharmacovigilance. The Summary Review does not explicitly attribute any change in the application to the AdComm; the only linkage is inferred (the committee's registry/PMSS discussion alongside the REMS with safety assessments that the review teams independently adopted).
